research.title: Cross-species surrogate to human transfer
research.body: Your pig-head FEM surrogate predicts brain strain from kinematics. Test whether a model trained on porcine simulations plus a small human set transfers via domain adaptation or physics-informed fine-tuning, and report calibration error against human instrumented-mouthguard cases.

research.title: Uncertainty-aware strain prediction
research.body: Most ML head-injury surrogates return a point estimate. Add conformal prediction or deep ensembles to give per-region strain intervals, then ask how often the interval flips an injury/no-injury call near the threshold.

research.title: Mouthguard kinematics error propagation
research.body: Quantify how sensor noise, coupling error and filtering in instrumented mouthguards propagate to regional brain strain through your pipeline. This produces a defensible error budget for field data.

research.title: Subject-specific meshes at scale with AnatoMesh
research.body: Run AnatoMesh over a public MRI cohort (age, sex, head size varied) and publish how anatomy variation shifts strain for the same impact. Fills the sex and age gap that most single-head-model studies leave open.

research.title: Cumulative exposure model for repetitive head impacts
research.body: Combine per-impact strain with a damage-accumulation or recovery term, calibrated to astrocyte reactivity in your animal data, to test whether many low-strain hits predict tissue pathology better than peak strain.

research.title: Link tissue pathology to simulated strain maps
research.body: Register histology (e.g. astrocyte segmentation outputs) to the simulated strain field and fit region-level dose-response curves. Extends your astrocyte segmentation tool into a mechanobiology result.

research.title: Blast versus impact loading in one framework
research.body: Use the same surrogate strategy for blast loading on the head. Few ML surrogates cover blast, and your cross-species angle suits large-animal blast data.

research.title: Biomarker-to-biomechanics bridge
research.body: Blood biomarkers (GFAP, UCH-L1, NfL) after known impact exposures could be regressed on simulated regional strain. A small athlete cohort with mouthguard plus blood draws would test it.

research.title: Benchmark and open leaderboard for head-injury surrogates
research.body: Publish a standard dataset of impact kinematics and simulated responses with fixed splits and metrics. Benchmarks attract citations and make your platform the reference.

market.title: Analytics layer for mouthguard vendors
market.body: Hardware vendors give kinematics; few give validated regional brain strain. A browser-based, no-install strain estimator (as your web surrogate already is) could be licensed or offered as an API.

market.title: Youth and high-school risk dashboards
market.body: Leagues with limited budgets want cumulative exposure tracking per player. Pair low-cost sensors with an exposure score and a coach-friendly dashboard. Needs a clear non-diagnostic disclaimer.

market.title: Helmet design and rating support
market.body: Helmet makers and rating labs can use fast surrogates to screen designs for rotational and strain metrics before physical testing. Offer a design-iteration service.

market.title: Insurance and litigation expert tooling
market.body: Reconstruction of head impacts from video or kinematics with strain estimates is used in expert reports. Validated, auditable pipelines are a niche with clear willingness to pay.

market.title: Military and blast exposure monitoring
market.body: Training-range blast exposure tracking is an active funding area. Surrogate models that map overpressure and kinematics to brain load fit defense SBIR-style calls.

market.title: Funding routes to watch
market.body: NIH (NINDS, NIBIB), DoD CDMRP, NFL and league-funded programs, NCAA-DoD CARE-type consortia, and SBIR/STTR for commercial spin-outs. Check current open calls before planning.

market.title: Open-source plus services model
market.body: Keep the core platforms open for citations and trust, and charge for hosted, validated, supported versions with regulatory-style documentation.
